{{Short description|German mathematician}}
{{Use dmy dates|cs1-dates=ly|date=May 2021}}
{{Use list-defined references|date=May 2021}}
'''Andrea Walther''' (born 1970<ref>{{cite web |title=DNB, Katalog der Deutschen Nationalbibliothek |url=https://portal.dnb.de/opac.htm?method=simpleSearch&cqlMode=true&query=nid%3D121832546 |website=portal.dnb.de |access-date=20 March 2026}}</ref> in Bremerhaven) is a German applied mathematician and professor of [[mathematical optimization]] in the department for mathematics of [[Humboldt University of Berlin]].

==Biography==
After completing an apprenticeship as a bank clerk at Deutsche Bank in Bremerhaven from 1989 to 1991, she studied business mathematics at the [[University of Bayreuth]], where she received her diploma in 1996.

Subsequently, Walther joined the [[DFG]] research group "Identification and Optimization of Complex Models Based on Analytical Sensitivities" at the [[TU Dresden]] as a research associate in analysis from 1997 to 1999. She earned her PhD in mathematics from TU Dresden in 1999.<ref name=":0">{{cite web|access-date=2026-03-18 |author=Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin |title=Short CV - Prof. Dr. Andrea Walther |url=https://www.mathematik.hu-berlin.de/en/research/fields-of-research/mathematische-optimierung/files_walther/walther-cv-e}}<!-- auto-translated from German by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> Her dissertation, ''Program Reversal Schedules for Single-and Multi-processor Machines'', was supervised by Andreas Griewank.<ref>{{cite web|access-date=2022-07-29 |title=Andrea Walther |url=https://mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=59123 |website=The Mathematics Genealogy Project}}<!-- auto-translated from German by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> From 2000 to 2002, she worked at the TU Dresden as a scientific assistant at the Institute of Mathematics.

Between 2003 and 2006, she led an independent junior research group on the analysis and optimization of computational models at TU Dresden. She was appointed Junior Professor in the same field at TU Dresden from 2007 to 2008. In 2007, she also served as a substitute professor ("Mathematics I") at the [[University of Regensburg]]. She completed her habilitation at TU Dresden in 2008.<ref  name=":0" />

From 2009 to 2019, Walther was Professor of Mathematics and its Applications at the [[University of Paderborn]]. Since 2019, she has been a MATH+ Professor of Mathematical Optimization in the department for mathematics at the Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin 2008.<ref  name=":0" />

From 2020 to 2022 Walther was convenor of the [[European Women in Mathematics]].<ref>[https://www.europeanwomeninmaths.org/andrea-walther-and-kaie-kubjas-elected-new-convenors/ Andrea Walther und Kaie Kubjas gewählte neue Convenors], European Women in Mathematics, 31. Juli 2020, Retrieved 2026-03-18</ref>

Since 2024, she has served as chair for the executive board of the Cluster of Excellence MATH+.<ref>[https://mathplus.de/about-us/mathplus-board/ MATH+ About Us], Retrieved 2026-03-18</ref> In the same year, she was appointed acting Vice President of the Zuse Institute Berlin.<ref>[https://www.zib.de/index.php/de/institut/ ZIB Organigramm], Retrieved 2026-03-18</ref>

== Research ==
Walther's research focuses on [[nonlinear programming]], nonsmooth optimization, [[scientific computing]], and algorithmic differentiation (also known as [[automatic differentiation]]). 

==Recognition==
Walther was elected as a Fellow of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]], in the 2025 Class of [[SIAM Fellow]]s, "for contributions in algorithmic optimization and automatic differentiation".<ref>[https://www.siam.org/publications/siam-news/articles/siam-announces-2025-class-of-fellows/], Retrieved 2026-03-20</ref> She gave an invited lecture at the 2023 SIAM Conference on Optimization in Seattle, USA.<ref>[https://meetings.siam.org/program.cfm?CONFCODE=OP23], Retrieved 2026-03-20</ref>

==Publications==

Walther has co-authored one book, three proceedings and  over 100 research papers.<ref>[https://scholar.google.com/citations?hl=de&user=0PRNV0oAAAAJ&view_op=list_works], Retrieved 2026-03-24</ref>

With Andreas Griewank, Walther published the text book ''Evaluating derivatives: principles and techniques of algorithmic differentiation'' ([[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]], 2008) on the theoretical foundation of Algorithmic Differentiation.<ref>[https://zbmath.org/1159.65026], Retrieved 2026-03-24</ref>
